SAMPLE LETTER FOR DEMONSTRATION. NOT A REAL NOTICE.

Sunshine Health
Florida Medicaid Managed Medical Assistance
Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination

Date: October 14, 2026
Member: J. Sample (age 9)
Member ID: 00000000-SAMPLE
Provider: Sample Home Nursing LLC

This letter is about the request for private duty nursing, 8 hours per day, service code T1000, for dates of service September 1, 2026 through September 30, 2026. The amount billed was $4,320.00.

We have denied this request. Reason: Services exceed the authorized amount. The plan approved fewer hours than were billed for this period.

You have the right to appeal this decision. Your appeal must be received within 60 days of the date of this letter, by December 13, 2026. You may ask for a copy of the rule we used and the records we reviewed at no cost.

This is a synthetic sample written for a software demonstration. It does not describe a real member, provider, or claim.

findings.question: Is private duty nursing covered under Florida Medicaid for children under 21?
findings.answer: Yes, Florida Medicaid covers private duty nursing for children under 21 who require more care than can be furnished through a home health visit. Services exceeding the policy or fee schedule may still be approved if medically necessary. The passages do not state the specific covered hours, visit limits, or authorization steps for private duty nursing.

citations.title: Florida Medicaid Home Health Services Coverage Policy (Rule 59G-4.130)
citations.quote: See the Florida Medicaid Personal Care Services and Private Duty Nursing Services Coverage Policies if the recipient is under the age of 21 years and requires more care than can be furnished through a home health visit.

citations.title: Florida Medicaid Private Duty Nursing and Family Home Health Aide Services Coverage Policy (Rule 59G-4.261)
citations.quote: As such, services for recipients under the age of 21 years exceeding the coverage described within this policy or the associated fee schedule may be approved, if medically necessary.

findings.question: What limits does Florida Medicaid place on how many hours of private duty nursing per day are allowed for children under 21?
findings.answer: Florida Medicaid covers up to 24 hours of PDN services per day, per recipient who requires more extensive and continual care than a home health visit and can be safely cared for at home or in the community under a licensed practitioner. When family home health aide services are also authorized, combined PDN and aide hours must not exceed 24 hours a day and the two services must not occur at the same time.

findings.question: Does Florida Medicaid require prior authorization or other approval conditions for private duty nursing for children under 21?
findings.answer: Yes — Florida Medicaid covers private duty nursing only at the skill level prescribed in the order and approved plan of care, and for recipients under 21 services exceeding the policy or fee schedule may be approved if medically necessary under the Authorization Requirements Policy. Under MMA the plan must provide case management for enrollees under 21 receiving Private Duty Nursing in the family home or other community-based setting, and does not cover PDN by an independent RN/LPN who is a related provider, legal guardian or caretaker relative, or PDN and family home health aide services provided concurrently. The passages do not state the step-by-step prior-authorization forms, timeframes, or numeric hour limits for private duty nursing.

findings.question: What is the Florida Medicaid appeal process, including the adverse benefit determination, how to file a grievance or appeal or request a fair hearing, the deadlines, and where to file?
findings.answer: Under MMA there are no additional general grievance and appeal or IRO provisions unique to MMA, and Title XXI MediKids enrollees are not eligible for the Medicaid Fair Hearing process. MMA plans must provide a notice of action to enrollees under age 21 in residential psychiatric treatment when fewer units or days are authorized after the initial authorization, and must provide pharmacy notice when prescription payment is denied under the Hernandez settlement. The passages do not state how to file a grievance, appeal, or fair hearing, the deadlines, or where to file.
